tasks.title: Drive the console-delete route in a sandbox and measure the Retry control
acceptance: C1 new driver (README 'Later runs in this directory': each run ships its own driver and leaves earlier ones untouched): `.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/driver/run-forced-load-failure.mjs` exists; at e539917 no path under `.dir-sdlc/handruns` contains `forced-load-failure` (`MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git -C C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate ls-tree -r --name-only e539917 -- .dir-sdlc/handruns | grep -c -i -E "forced-load-failure|HUMANCHECKS"` printed 0 at authoring). It imports `launch`/`repoRoot` from `./lib.mjs` and `buildSandbox` from `./sandbox.mjs`, and no file under `driver/` other than this one differs from e539917 (orchestrator: `git diff --name-only e539917 <task tip> -- .dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/driver` lists exactly this one path; quoted into `reviews/T1.md`).

C2 build: `npm --prefix <worktree> run build` exits 0 in the worktree and leaves `<worktree>/out/main/index.js`; the committed `driven-report-forced-load-failure.json` `meta.mainBundleSha256` equals `sha256sum <worktree>/out/main/index.js` as it stood when the run was made (the implementer records both in its report). Not run at authoring, because it writes `out/`; the orchestrator probes it before the freeze (see the architect report).

C3 invocation, usage error: `node <worktree>/.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/driver/run-forced-load-failure.mjs --bogus` exits 2 and writes no report and no screenshot; likewise with `--sandbox-root` absent, and with `--sandbox-root relative/dir`. The implementer reports each of the three exit codes, and a listing taken before and after each shows no `driven-report-forced-load-failure*` file and no `screenshots/forced-load-failure*` directory created or changed.

C4 invocation, normal and skip-delete: `--sandbox-root <absolute dir>` is required; without `--skip-delete` the run's slug is `forced-load-failure`, with it `forced-load-failure-skip-delete`; a run writes only `driven-report-<slug>.json`, `driven-report-<slug>.md`, `screenshots/<slug>/*.png` and the sandbox root, and removes the sandbox root at exit unless `--keep-sandbox` is passed. The session's own runs pass a sandbox root inside the implementer's scratch directory (Hard rule: writes stay in the worktree or scratch); `meta.sandboxRoot` records it.

C5 sandbox isolation (README 'Safety'; precedent every earlier driver): the app is launched with `buildSandbox(<sandbox root>).env` (USERPROFILE, HOME, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, TEMP, TMP redirected, `driver/sandbox.mjs`); `meta` records the sha256 of the real `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json` read before launch and after exit (or `absent` both times), and the two are equal in both committed reports.

C6 binding the run to the file: each committed report's `meta.driverSha256` equals `sha256sum` of the committed `driver/run-forced-load-failure.mjs`, and `meta` also records `generatedAt`, the Electron and Playwright versions, `slug` and `exitCode`.

C7 plan before run (precedent `run-fork-ui.mjs` RULES): every observation O2-O14 named below has, in a PLAN literal in the driver written before anything runs, its prediction and its in-window control with that control's prediction; the JSON report carries per observation `id`, `backlogRow` (`retry-button` or `retry-themes`), `verdict` (`pass`, `fail` or `instrument-invalid`), `measured`, `control.injection`, `control.predicted`, `control.observed`, `fired` and `undoVerified`; a measurement still `null` at its comparison makes the verdict `instrument-invalid`, never `pass`; a control that did not fire as predicted makes it `instrument-invalid` whatever was measured.

C8 state S1, setup: through `window.orcastrate.pods.create({ title, cwd, permissionMode: 'default' })` (`src/preload/api.ts:95`) the run creates three Pods in this order, titled `HC load companion`, `HC load live`, `HC load target`, each with an existing sandbox directory as `cwd`; it then reloads the renderer and waits for the three `pod-tab:<id>` tabs (`src/renderer/src/contracts/renderer-view.ts:401-402`). The report records each Pod's id and tab order.

C9 O1 precondition, auto-activation: after the reload, the selected Pod tab is `HC load companion` (first by tab order, `src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:629-633`), so neither `HC load live` nor `HC load target` has been activated. Measured from the DOM's selected-tab state. O1 is a precondition and carries no control; if the selected tab is any other, O2-O14 are `instrument-invalid`.

C10 O2 the delete leaves a stale tab: `window.orcastrate.pods.delete({ podId: <HC load target id>, deleteSession: false })` (`src/preload/api.ts:100`) resolves `ok: true` with `podDeleted: true` and `session: 'not-requested'` (`src/main/ipc/handlers.ts:152-158`), and afterwards the `pod-tab:<target id>` tab is still rendered. Control: the same tab-presence probe for a never-created id (a fresh UUID) reports absent.

C11 (prediction, met per C24) O3 E8 and E9 are raised: before the target is clicked, `HC load live`'s tab is clicked (its loads succeed); then the target's stale tab is clicked, and, waited for as a condition with a timeout (no fixed sleep, test discipline 'Determinism'), exactly 2 elements `[data-testid="notification"][data-kind="error"]` (`src/renderer/src/notifications/types.ts:70`, `NotificationItem.tsx:64-65`) are present whose message `

` text equals `no Pod with id ` (main's message, `src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts:1657`). Prediction: 2. Its in-window control is O4; its whole-run control is C25.

C12 (prediction, met per C24) O4the live Pod raises nothing (must-not-fire control for O3): measured at the moment O3's two items are present, the number of notification items whose text contains `HC load live`'s id is 0, and the total number of `data-kind="error"` items is exactly 2. Prediction: 0 and 2. Control: the same id-containment count, keyed on the target's id instead of `HC load live`'s, reports 2 at the same moment. (The live Pod's reads were issued before the target's, so they have answered by then; the FINDINGS file says so.)

C13 (prediction, met per C24) O5each item carries one Retry button: each of O3's two items contains exactly one `button` element with `type="button"` and text `Retry`, and in DOM order it follows the message `

` and precedes the `notification-dismiss` button (`src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationItem.tsx:77-95`). Control: the same probe on the item with its Retry button temporarily detached reports 0 buttons; reattached and verified.

C14 (prediction, met per C24) O6Retry is drawn as its own control (backlog row `retry-button`, 'reads as a button'): for the first item's Retry, computed `border-top-style` is `solid` with a width greater than 0, `cursor` is `pointer`, and its computed `background-color` differs from the item's. Control: inline `border-style: none; background: transparent` on that button makes the probe report no border and an equal background; undone and verified.

C15 (prediction, met per C24) O7Retry sits beside the message: the Retry button's border box starts at or right of the message `

`'s right edge, within one device pixel (`1 / devicePixelRatio`, read in the window), and their vertical extents overlap. Control: inline `flex-direction: column` on the item makes the probe report no horizontal adjacency; undone and verified.

C16 (prediction, met per C24) O8Tab reaches Retry with focus-visible: using keyboard `Tab` presses only (no programmatic `focus()`), from a stated starting point, `document.activeElement` becomes the first item's Retry button and `el.matches(':focus-visible')` is true; the report records the starting point and the number of presses. Control: before the presses, the same probe reports the button not focused.

C17 (prediction, met per C24) O9the ring is painted (frontend discipline 'Focus is visible'): with Retry focused as in O8, computed `outline-style` is `solid` and `outline-width` equals `--oc-border-thick` resolved in the same window (`Notifications.module.css:79-81`, token at `tokens.css:164`), and a clip capture of the ring's rectangle differs from the same clip captured with Retry unfocused. Control: an added `<style>` giving that one button `outline: none !important` makes the probe report `none` and two byte-identical captures; removed and verified.

C18 (prediction, met per C24) O10the ring stays inside the item: the ring's outer rectangle (Retry's border box inflated by `outline-offset` plus `outline-width`) lies within the item's padding box, so it neither reaches nor crosses the item's border. Control: inline `padding: 0` on the item makes the probe report the ring outside the padding box; undone and verified.

C19 (prediction, met per C24) O11no ancestor clips the ring: for every ancestor of the Retry button up to the document root whose computed `overflow-x` or `overflow-y` is not `visible`, the ring's outer rectangle lies within that ancestor's padding box; the report lists the ancestors checked. Control: inline `overflow: hidden; padding: 0` on the item makes the probe report a clipping ancestor; undone and verified.

C20 (prediction, met per C24) O12legible under the dark preference: with `win.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })`, the contrast ratio of Retry's computed `color` against its effective background is at least 4.5 (the threshold `run-fork-ui.mjs` O12 used); foreground, background and ratio recorded. Control: inline `color` set to the measured background gives ratio 1.00; undone and verified.

C21 (prediction, met per C24) O13legible under the light preference: as C20 with `colorScheme: 'light'`, ratio at least 4.5; foreground, background and ratio recorded. Control as C20, under the light preference.

C22 (prediction, met per C24) O14the preference changes nothing (single palette, `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:14-16`): Retry's computed `color`, `background-color`, `border-top-color` and the item's `background-color` under the light preference each equal their values under the dark preference. Control: an added `<style>` containing `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` that sets Retry's `color` to a fixed distinct value makes the probe report a difference under light and none under dark; removed and verified. `emulateMedia` is reset to `null` afterwards.

C23 screenshots for Gate 3: `screenshots/forced-load-failure/` holds at least four PNGs, named so the preference and focus state can be read from the name: the notification viewport unfocused and with Retry focused, under the dark and the light preference each; the JSON report lists each path, and each listed path exists in the worktree.

C24 exit code and the measurement rule: the driver exits 0 if and only if every observation is `pass` and every control fired, and non-zero otherwise; the committed `driven-report-forced-load-failure.json` records the exit code of the run it reports, whatever it was. The verdicts are reported as measured, not as predicted. Each of C11-C22 states its observation's prediction, and each is met when, in the committed `forced-load-failure` report, that observation's verdict is `pass` or `fail` (never `instrument-invalid`), its control fired as predicted, and its undo is verified. A `fail` verdict is a finding for Gate 3, not an unmet criterion, and FINDINGS reports it as measured.

C25 the must-fail run: `--skip-delete` performs C8-C9 and clicks the target's tab without deleting it; in its committed `driven-report-forced-load-failure-skip-delete.json`, O3 is `fail` with 0 matching error items within the timeout, and `meta.exitCode` is non-zero.

C26 controls leave nothing behind: every control that ran, in either committed report, has `undoVerified: true` before the next observation runs (in the `--skip-delete` run, observations after O3 may record no control as run), and no control edits a file (inline styles, an added `<style>`, a detached node, emulated media only).

C27 findings file: `FINDINGS-FORCED-LOAD-FAILURE.md` exists with a verdict table carrying one row per observation of the `forced-load-failure` run (id, backlog row, verdict, measured, control, control observed, fired), a section on the `forced-load-failure-skip-delete` run, and a summary; it says how O3's two items are attributed to E8 and E9 (the DOM carries no key) with its evidence (`src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.tsx:95-103`, the two `usePodLoadAlert` calls), and that no route forces E10.

C28 no backlog line numbers in the findings file: `grep -cE 'backlog\.md:[0-9]' <worktree>/.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/FINDINGS-FORCED-LOAD-FAILURE.md` prints 0. Control: the same command over `C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.sir/sessions/20261110-1618-chrome-alert-squeeze/spec.md` printed 3 at authoring.

C29 harness copy (lesson 2026-11-09): where the harness blocks this task's edit tools for a file it owns, the task writes that file's full text into its own scratch directory and its report asks the orchestrator to copy it in; the report gives the sha256 handed over, and it equals `sha256sum` of the file in the worktree, recorded in `reviews/T1.md`. Where the driver itself is blocked, the task stops after writing it to scratch, and is re-dispatched to run it once the copy has landed, because `lib.mjs` derives `repoRoot` from the driver's own location (`driver/lib.mjs:7-8`).

C30 no production change: the task's commit touches no path under `src/` or `tests/` (orchestrator: `git diff --name-only e539917 <task tip> -- src tests` prints nothing; quoted into `reviews/T1.md`).

tasks.title: Write the human-checks recipe for the two Retry-control backlog rows
acceptance: C1 the file exists: `.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/HUMANCHECKS-FORCED-LOAD-FAILURE.md` exists (absent at e539917, see T1 C1's command). Counted with `python -I -X utf8`, it has exactly one line each equal to `## Before you start: this runs against your real data`, `## Setup` and `## Cleanup`, and exactly two lines matching `^## H[12] `, in the order Setup, H1, H2, Cleanup.

C2 each check's shape (precedent `docs/human-checks/chrome-alert-width.md`): counted with `python -I -X utf8` per section, each of H1 and H2 has at least one line matching `^[0-9]+\. `, exactly one line beginning `**Passes when:**` and exactly one line beginning `**Backlog:**`.

C3 start: a numbered Setup step tells the user to run `npm run dev` in the repository root, naming the session worktree `.claude-worktrees/20261117-1751-forced-load-failure` before the merge and the main checkout after it.

C4 console: a Setup step says how to open the developer tools console: `Control+Shift+I`, or `Alt` to show the hidden menu bar (`autoHideMenuBar: true`, `src/main/window.ts:21`) then View, Toggle Developer Tools, then the Console tab; it says this rests on Electron's default menu (the app sets no `Menu` in `src/`) and was not run in this session.

C5 titles are free: before creating anything, a step runs `(await window.orcastrate.pods.list()).value.map((p) => [p.title, p.id])` (`src/preload/api.ts:94`) and tells the user to stop if any Pod is already titled `HC load companion` or `HC load target`.

C6 create: steps create two Pods with `await window.orcastrate.pods.create({ title, cwd, permissionMode: 'default' })` (`src/preload/api.ts:95`), `HC load companion` first and `HC load target` second, with `cwd` an absolute path to a folder that already exists (a relative path is refused, `src/main/ipc/validate.ts:106-108`; a missing folder is CWD_MISSING, `src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts:419-421`); they tell the user to note the `id` the target's call returns.

C7 why two, and do not click: the file says the first Pod by tab order is activated on load (`src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:629-633`) and activation loads only once per Pod (`store.ts:798`), so the target must be a later tab and must not be clicked before the delete step.

C8 reload: a step reloads the window with `location.reload()` typed in the console, and says why: a Pod created from the console is not added to the window's list, which is read at start-up (`src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:374`).

C9 confirm, then delete (project lesson 2026-11-11): the delete step's command selects the Pod from a fresh `pods.list()` by the exact title `HC load target` and calls `window.orcastrate.pods.delete({ podId, deleteSession: false })` (`src/preload/api.ts:100`) only when exactly one Pod has that title, printing a refusal otherwise; a step before it prints that Pod's id and tells the user to check it, character for character, against the id noted in C6's step before pressing Enter; and the file warns that the call asks for no confirmation and cannot be undone.

C10 side effects (project lesson 2026-11-11): the 'Before you start' section names, for each step that runs a command or changes data, what it writes, with a `file:line` each: starting the app (start-up reconciliation, `src/main/index.ts:135`, `src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts:316-358`); `pods.list` (reads only); `pods.create` (one new row, status `closed`, its tab order the count of existing Pods, `created_at` and `last_active_at` now; no other row, no process started, no file in the Claude home: `pod-manager.ts:418-431`, `src/main/store/sqlite-event-store.ts:167-193`); `location.reload()` (the window only; main keeps running, so no start-up reconciliation); `pods.delete` with `deleteSession: false` (no runner to stop, `pod-manager.ts:1015-1017`; the row is deleted and its lanes and events with it, `sqlite-event-store.ts:238-244`; no conversation file is touched, `src/main/ipc/handlers.ts:152-158`; the window is not told, so the tab stays); clicking the stale tab and Retry (reads that fail, nothing written, `pod-manager.ts:1114-1131`, `:1655-1658`); and the Cleanup deletions. It states that no step in this file other than starting the app rewrites another Pod's row, and that no step rewrites any `last_active_at`.

C11 H1 the Retry button and its ring: steps click the target's stale tab and say what appears: two error notifications at the window's bottom-right, each reading `no Pod with id <id>` (`src/main/pod-manager/pod-manager.ts:1657`), with a `Retry` button between the message and the × (`src/renderer/src/notifications/NotificationItem.tsx:77-95`); then the keyboard route to Retry that T1's O8 used, what the ring is (`.action:focus-visible`, `Notifications.module.css:79-81`) and what 'clipped by the item's border' would look like; and that Retry fails again and the notification comes back under the same key (`src/renderer/src/shell/WorkspaceAlerts.tsx:15-23`). **Backlog** names `20261112-0151-workspace-load-retry` and the words "reads as a button next to the message".

C12 H2 the two themes: the section states that Orcastrate has one colour palette and no light theme (`src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.css:14-16`; a single `:root` block, held by `src/renderer/src/styles/tokens.test.ts:85-87`; the only `prefers-color-scheme` text in `src/` is that comment: `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 git -C C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate grep -n -E "prefers-color-scheme" e539917 -- src` printed 1 line, `tokens.css:15`, at authoring, while the near-miss `prefers-reduced-motion` matched lines in 7 files); it gives at least one way to switch the light/dark preference the window sees, says for each whether it was run in this session, and tells the user what to compare under each. **Backlog** names `20261112-0151-workspace-load-retry` and the words "visible and legible in both the light and the dark theme".

C13 the driven results are cited: H1 quotes the `forced-load-failure` run's verdicts and measured values for O5-O11 and H2 for O12-O14, from `driven-report-forced-load-failure.json`, each with its O-id, and each section names at least two screenshots from `screenshots/forced-load-failure/`; counted with `python -I -X utf8`, every path in the file ending `.png` resolves to a file under `.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/` in the worktree, and there are at least 4 distinct such paths.

C14 E10: the file states that no step forces E10, because main answers `app.routingMode` from a value it already holds (`src/main/ipc/handlers.ts:239`) and the window reads it at start-up (`src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:430`), and that neither backlog row needs E10.

C15 Cleanup: steps reload the window first (the stale target tab then disappears; its × would fail, because main no longer has the Pod and the window's delete returns that failure, `src/renderer/src/state/store.ts:700-701`), then delete `HC load companion` with its × (named `Delete HC load companion`, `src/renderer/src/pods/PodTab.tsx:385`) and **Delete** in the dialog, with the checkbox left unticked (it defaults off, `src/renderer/src/pods/DeletePodDialog.tsx:87`); then stop `npm run dev` with `Control+C` and close that terminal (lesson 2026-11-16, the worktree folder cannot be removed while it is open).

C16 no backlog line numbers: `grep -cE 'backlog\.md:[0-9]' <worktree>/.dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/HUMANCHECKS-FORCED-LOAD-FAILURE.md` prints 0. Control: the same command over `C:/Users/dmarq/Development/Repos/orcastrate/.sir/sessions/20261110-1618-chrome-alert-squeeze/spec.md` printed 3 at authoring.

C17 every `src/...:<line>` the file cites holds what the file says it holds, checked against the worktree's copy, which this session leaves unchanged (T1 C30); the implementer lists each citation it checked in its report.

C18 README entry: `README.md`'s 'Later runs in this directory' list gains one bullet naming `FINDINGS-FORCED-LOAD-FAILURE.md` and `HUMANCHECKS-FORCED-LOAD-FAILURE.md`, the slugs `forced-load-failure` and `forced-load-failure-skip-delete`, and each run's exit code and pass count as the committed reports record them.

C19 README otherwise unchanged: every line of `README.md` at e539917 is still present, in order, in the task's `README.md` (orchestrator: `git diff e539917 <task tip> -- .dir-sdlc/handruns/2026-09-30-electron-handrun/README.md` shows no removed line; quoted into `reviews/T2.md`).

C20 harness copy (lesson 2026-11-09): where the harness blocks this task's edit tools for either file, the task writes the file's full text into its own scratch directory and its report asks the orchestrator to copy it in; the report gives the sha256 handed over, and it equals `sha256sum` of the file in the worktree, recorded in `reviews/T2.md`.
